exercises.title: Run the purpose test
exercises.intro: Run six borrowers through our purpose screen and see where each file lands. Pick a case, then answer each question in turn.

start.q: Is the borrower an entity: an LLC, LP or corporation?

options.label: No, an individual or a trust

occupancy.q: Will an owner, guarantor or relative live in the property for more than 14 days in the coming year?

cashout.q: Is this a refinance with cash out?

options.label: No, a purchase or a refinance with no cash out

personal.q: Will more than half of the cash out go to personal, family or household use?

decline_entity.result: Decline: the borrower is not an entity
decline_entity.explain: Only LLCs, LPs and corporations may borrow (CORE-BOR-01). Reg Z may still deem some owner-occupied loans to individuals business purpose, but our policy declines them first [VERIFY: Reg Z comment 3(a)-5; checked 20 Nov 2026].

stop_occupancy.result: Stop the file: occupancy red flag
stop_occupancy.explain: More than 14 days makes the property owner-occupied [VERIFY: Reg Z comment 3(a)-4; checked 20 Nov 2026]. No guarantor or relative may live in a 1-4 unit property (CORE-BP-02). No exception is allowed (CORE-EXC-03). In Ohio, family occupancy can also bring the loan under consumer licensing (SLT-OH-01).

decline_cashout.result: Decline: consumer purpose by use of proceeds
decline_cashout.explain: More than half of the cash out is for personal use, so the loan is treated as consumer purpose (CORE-BP-04). No exception is allowed (CORE-EXC-03).

business.explain: The borrower is an entity, no owner or relative lives there, and any cash out is half or less personal. Credit to a non-natural person is exempt from TILA [VERIFY: 12 CFR 1026.3(a); checked 22 Nov 2026]. Credit for rental property the owner does not occupy is deemed business purpose [VERIFY: Reg Z comment 3(a)-4; checked 20 Nov 2026]. Every borrower and guarantor signs the purpose certificate (CORE-BP-01).

cases.text: Cedar Court Partners LLC buys a 50-unit apartment building in Charlotte to renovate and rent (RD-MF-01).
Birchwood Plaza LLC buys a 70%-leased strip center in Indianapolis (RD-COM-01).
An individual buys a duplex and will live in one unit.
An LLC buys a single-family rental. Its managing member plans to stay there 3 weeks each summer.
Harborline Holdings LLC buys Maple Run, but Dana Reyes's sister will live there for the winter.
An LLC refinances a rental with $90,000 cash out. $46,000 is for personal use.

exercises.title: Build Cedar Court's purpose file
exercises.intro: A purpose file must hang together. Decide which documents belong in Cedar Court's purpose file, and which are not purpose documents for this deal.

items.text: Business-purpose and non-occupancy certificate signed by Cedar Court Partners LLC, Marcus Hale and Priya Nand
items.why: The borrower and every guarantor sign it (CORE-BP-01). Both owners hold 20% or more, so both guarantee.

items.text: Cedar Court Partners LLC formation documents and a North Carolina good-standing certificate
items.why: They show the borrower is an entity, so only an entity borrows (CORE-BOR-01).

items.text: The State Law Table check for North Carolina (SLT-NC-02), done before the term sheet
items.why: The property state's row is checked before any term sheet (CORE-BP-03).

items.text: ID for Marcus Hale and Priya Nand, with proof of home addresses other than the property
items.why: ID is a KYC check (CORE-KYC-02). A separate home address supports non-occupancy (CORE-BP-02).

items.text: The lender-ordered MAI appraisal, showing 44 of 50 units leased
items.why: The appraisal shows occupancy and condition, so it can confirm or contradict purpose (CORE-VAL-01).

items.text: A written use-of-proceeds statement for cash out
items.why: CORE-BP-04 applies only to a refinance with cash out. Cedar Court is a purchase.
It is a required property report (MF-GEN-08), but it says nothing about loan purpose.

items.text: The rate cap confirmation, strike 4.25% for 24 months
items.why: The cap manages floating-rate risk (MF-BR-09). It is a closing condition, not purpose evidence.

exercises.title: Cash-out boundary
exercises.intro: CORE-BP-04 declines a cash-out refinance when more than half goes to personal use. Test cases at 50%, 51.11%, 58.33% and 62.5%, plus one with no statement and one with no cash out.

start.q: Is the loan a refinance with cash out?

statement.q: Has the borrower stated the use of proceeds in writing?

share.q: Personal use ÷ total cash out. Is the result more than 50.00%?

not_applicable.explain: The use-of-proceeds test covers only refinances with cash out (CORE-BP-04). Run the rest of the purpose screen as usual.

get_statement.result: Stop: get the written statement first
get_statement.explain: On any refinance with cash out, the borrower states the use of proceeds in writing (CORE-BP-04). You cannot run the test without it.

decline.explain: More than half of the cash out goes to personal, family or household use. The loan is treated as consumer purpose and declined (CORE-BP-04). No exception is allowed (CORE-EXC-03).

proceed.explain: Exactly half is not more than half, so the test does not decline it (CORE-BP-04). Keep the statement and evidence for the business use in the file.

cases.text: An LLC refinances a rental with $90,000 cash out, and $46,000 is for personal use. A signed statement is on file.
An LLC refinances with $100,000 cash out: $50,000 to pay off a member's car loan and $50,000 for roof repairs. A signed statement is on file.
An LLC refinances with $120,000 cash out: $70,000 for a member's home renovation and $50,000 for the next flip. A signed statement is on file.
An LLC refinances with $80,000 cash out, of which $50,000 is personal. A signed statement is on file.
An LLC refinances with $90,000 cash out. The borrower has not yet said how it will use the money.
Harborline Holdings LLC buys Maple Run for $300,000. There is no refinance.
